description: Default configuration for repositories in the Webinertia organisation

packageRules.description: Webware components always move to the latest release, so replace the constraint with the new floor instead of widening it. Widening turns a constraint into an OR-range (^1.0 || ^2.0), which prefer-stable then resolves back to the older stable line, and which grows a duplicate alternative on the next release (^1.0 || ^2.0 || ^2.0).
Webware components: group updates and track their prereleases

Docker images: own group, automerge patches and minors. The separate group is required, not cosmetic: group:allNonMajor groups every ecosystem into one branch, and a branch only automerges when every upgrade in it is automergeable, so a Docker update sharing a branch with a Composer update would never automerge. Majors stay manual via :separateMajorReleases, and rollbacks carry their own updateType so they are never matched here.

PHP tooling image: follow the 8.4 and 8.5 lines. The ^8.4.1 range on the php rule above excludes every 8.5 release, which capped the tooling image at 8.4 and, because rollbackPrs is enabled, would propose rolling 8.5 back down.
PHP tooling image: patch only for automerge. A PHP minor moves the analyser and the CI target at the same time, so it stays a deliberate edit.

MySQL is pinned to the 9.7 LTS line on purpose. Docker tags carry no LTS/innovation distinction, so a higher number reads as a routine major bump and silently moves the dev database onto the innovation track: mysql:26.7 is innovation while the image's own lts tag resolves to 9.7.2. Patches within 9.7 are still proposed; changing lines must be a deliberate edit, not a Renovate PR.
